name: C++ 10 — Practice Lab (File Handling and a Persistent Box Office)
description: Guided learner workspace for the tenth lab of a beginner C++ course (3×45 min) on file handling and the persistent storage of the box office. First block — fundamentals: a stock snapshot written with ofstream, with the open, buffer and close checks afterwards (G10_01_save), appending and summing visitor counts with a read loop (G10_02_visitors), invalid data and the stream state flags eof/fail (G10_03_invalid_data), then strict validation of one record line through getline and istringstream (G10_04_line). Second block — project: the box office carried over from lesson 9 (P10_box_office.cpp holds the base operations, the new file I/O is the student's work) built up in six steps, P1–P6 (understanding the base and the shared TICKETS 1 file format, saving with a header, parsing one reservation line, all-or-nothing loading into a temporary object, a text report built with ostringstream, then a save-or-load main driven by S or L plus the supplied broken-file fixtures). Third block — summary test: 20 fixed questions (T1 10 multiple-choice, T2 5 output prediction and 5 debugging) with feedback and no answer key in the student package. Before every part the tutor shows a short analogous sample from the EXAMPLES.md collection; the student writes, saves, compiles and runs the code (RUN button or g++ -std=c++20), and progress is tracked in PROGRESS.json. No homework and no separate extra exercise set.
